problem: Prior R2R VLN models (building on an entity-aware graph-attention model) lose visual information and struggle to match instruction entities (scene, object, direction) with visual features, which leads to overshooting the goal.
motivation: Instructions contain many entity clues such as objects, scenes and directions. Explicitly making the agent object-aware should improve cross-modal matching and navigation accuracy in domestic environments.
key_idea: Add object features to the LSTM state input under different fusion strategies, and combine them with entity-aware attention over object, scene and direction contexts and a visual attention graph, to build an object-aware VLN agent.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The authors claim object awareness reduces visual information loss and alleviates overshooting.
method: Object feature injection: adds object features (with several fusion strategies) to the LSTM input used to infer the robot state.
Language attention: extracts specialized and relational contexts of object, scene and direction entities from the instruction.
Visual attention graph: built to obtain entity aspects from vision and derive the navigation action.
Two-stage hierarchical training: first stage uses imitation plus reinforcement learning; second stage fine-tunes with augmentation data to improve generalization.

setting.backbone: LSTM-based entity-aware VLN model with attention and a visual attention graph (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: R2R training data, plus augmentation data for second-stage fine-tuning
setting.observation: panoramic RGB with object features (per abstract; details not given)

results: The abstract states OVLN improves SR and SPL over previous methods on R2R and alleviates overshoot, but gives no numbers.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so quantitative results and ablations could not be verified.
Evaluated only on R2R in a discrete simulator; no real-robot evidence despite the domestic-robot framing.
builds_on: Entity-aware/graph-attention VLN model (ref [1], likely Hong et al. 2020)
